proof: The agent read a random value created only inside the browser shell, wrote a report there, and verified it. A human terminal command read the same report.
checks: Actual native directory handle and browser write-permission approval
Real Claude agent with only Read/Write tools created and verified a browser-shell report
Browser stayed offline during connection, agent execution, and verification
Remote output preserves the local unfinished command and cursor
Duplicate request IDs do not execute twice
Requests for another session are ignored
Partially written JSON does not execute and does not break the connection
A request-file replacement gap does not disconnect the session
Disconnect closes the file session and stops command processing
Reconnecting a recognized folder preserves extra files
The stop button interrupts an agent command and closes its folder connection
additionalFolderGuards: Unrelated files, malformed session metadata, and an active session were rejected without writes.
limits: The browser and agent must have access to the same folder.
Native directory drag-and-drop and the browser write-permission prompt were tested with desktop Playwright Chromium.
The native directory picker alternative was unreliable in the Linux test environment and is not considered validated.
The interruption check restored connectivity before the shell reset, which reloads static engine assets.
Agent usage is one run reported by the CLI, not a general cost estimate or billing receipt.
